title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Papua New Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Papua New Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Papua New Guinea: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in Papua New Guinea, administrative steps span hospital cause-of-death reporting, registration with the PNG Civil and Identity Registry (PNGCIR), superannuation death claims, National Court or Public Trustee estate administration, and Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) tax clearances [1][4][6][8]. Following statutory forms and notice windows avoids delays across provincial centres and Port Moresby.

steps.title: Medical certification, emergency reporting, and employer transport duties
steps.html:
• Call emergency medical line 111 (or #115 toll-free / +675 324 8100 / +675 324 8200 for Port Moresby General Hospital) if urgent hospital or ambulance coordination is needed [11]. Obtain the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death from the attending medical officer, or wait for police and coronial clearance if the death was sudden or unexplained [4][5][12].
  • If the person who died was employed under an attested contract or employment arrangement covered by the Employment Act 1978 (Cap. 373), the employer must notify a labour officer at the first practicable opportunity (Section 27) and route unpaid wages through the labour officer where required (Section 84(3)) [13].
  • Under Sections 42 and 42A of the Employment Act 1978, where a worker or accompanying dependant brought to the place of employment dies before repatriation, the employer must on family request cover the cost of a coffin and transport of the body to the usual place of abode, as well as repatriate dependants [13].

steps.title: Civil death registration under the Civil and Identity Registration framework
steps.html:
• File the official Information of Death form and medical cause-of-death documentation through the PNG Civil and Identity Registry (PNGCIR) under the Civil and Identity Registration Act (modernizing the earlier Civil Registration Act 1963) [4][5][6].
  • Observe the statutory 21-day reporting window governing death and burial or remains-disposal notifications by health facility heads, medical attendants, and persons carrying out burials [5][6].
  • Order multiple official certified Death Certificate extracts immediately for superannuation funds, commercial banks, National Court probate filings, and consular use [3][7][12].

steps.title: Superannuation death claims (Nasfund and Nambawan Super)
steps.html:
• Notify the deceased person's superannuation fund promptly using certified Death Certificates, claimant identity verification, and marriage or birth proofs for dependants or nominated beneficiaries [7][8].
  • For Nasfund members (+675 313 1800 / shortcode 1588 / help@nasfund.com.pg), check beneficiary nomination files and submit death claim forms through e-Branch or service centres [7].
  • For Nambawan Super Limited members (180 1599 toll-free, Monday to Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM), contact Member Services and review beneficiary distribution guidelines for public- and private-sector contributors [8][9].

steps.title: Probate, Office of the Public Trustee, and Internal Revenue Commission (IRC)
steps.html:
• Assess estate assets under the Wills Act and the Wills, Probate and Administration Act 1966 (paclii.org) to apply to the National Court for a Grant of Probate (with a valid Will) or Letters of Administration (on intestacy) [1][2].
  • Where institutional administration is needed, no executor acts locally, or minors/vulnerable beneficiaries require fiduciary protection, contact Office of the Public Trustee (+675-301-2800, publictrustee@justice.gov.pg) within the Department of Justice and Attorney General, operating under the Public Curator Act (Cap. 81) and 2020 Amendment [3].
  • File final personal income tax returns and obtain any required Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC) through Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) (irc.gov.pg) before transferring substantial funds or clearing business registrations [10][15]. PNG does not impose a separate inheritance or estate tax [10].

steps.title: Consular legalisation and notifying banks and institutions
steps.html:
• Because Papua New Guinea is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, PNG Death Certificates and National Court grants needed overseas require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than an Apostille [14]. Confirm authentication and translation requirements with the foreign embassy or receiving registry before dispatching originals abroad [12][14].
  • Notify PNG commercial banks, employers, motor registries, insurers, and provincial land authorities in writing with certified Death Certificates and court grants [1][3][13].
  • Retain complete copies of PNGCIR registration receipts, super fund payout letters, and IRC tax clearances [4][7][10].
